page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance reaches 3442.17, placing it in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also perform in the top tier, with gzip compression at 37.65 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 16.7 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 13769.99 and a PassMark CPU score of 17535.04, both falling into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 48.64 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 26.09 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1:4, making it suitable for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and database operations. In benchmark testing, static web serving throughput reached 26.51 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations achieved 14.96 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, the instance demonstrates a tradeoff: it achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 340.98 tokens per second for small (135M) LLM models, but prompt processing for medium (7B) models is weak at 30.28 tokens per second. Given the lack of local NVMe storage and GPUs, workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O or hardware acceleration are not supported.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, it features a 32 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, the n4d-standard-8 demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and small-model LLM text generation. However, its multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and medium-model LLM prompt processing fall into average or weak categories. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from strong single-thread execution but do not require local NVMe storage or hardware acceleration.
